title: [FeatureRequest] Add ability to link with local generation services (ComfyUI, etc)
author: Tsubashi
body:
As far as I can tell, ArtCraft currently only operates with cloud-provided generation services. I've already set up local generation via ComfyUI, and it would be great to be able to hook into that. I recognize that implementing this isn't as simple as toggling a switch or configuration option, but I still think it would be worthwhile. It would broaden the project's appeal and hopefully attract power-users who can help contribute to the project. 

In terms of actually getting it working, I think I would break it into three parts. First, the adapter that would send the information from the GUI to the local service. Second, the pieces that would plug in on the local side (ie. custom ComfyUI Nodes). Lastly, the changes to the GUI to allow for local services to be added and configured.

title: Feature Request: An Adobe Encore Alternative for DVD/Blu-ray Authoring
author: renji-toda
body:
I would like to suggest a future ArtCraft application for **DVD-Video and Blu-ray authoring**, as a modern alternative to Adobe Encore.

Adobe Encore CS6 is still one of the best tools I have found for creating highly customized DVD/Blu-ray menus, but it has been discontinued for many years. Unfortunately, most modern alternatives sacrifice creative freedom for template-based menus.

What I am looking for is not simply software that can "burn a DVD/Blu-ray", but an authoring tool where the creator can **design the entire menu and then define its behavior**.

### Key features

* DVD-Video and Blu-ray authoring
* DVD ISO and Blu-ray ISO output
* Import custom menu backgrounds
* Import custom button artwork
* Freely position buttons
* Assign arbitrary navigation links to buttons
* Button highlight states
* Separate main/title menus and chapter/scene menus
* Multiple levels of menu navigation
* Still-image, video, and audio menu backgrounds
* Chapter/scene selection
* Ideally, one project that can produce both DVD and Blu-ray versions

The most important principle would be:

> **The software should provide the authoring engine, while the creator controls the design.**

In other words, the user should not be restricted to predefined menu templates. A menu designed in Photoshop or another graphics application should be usable essentially as designed, with author-defined interactive areas and navigation.

I believe there is still a real need for this. Adobe Encore and DVD Architect demonstrated that there is a market for highly customizable disc authoring, but both are now discontinued. Most current consumer tools can create DVDs and Blu-rays, but their menu systems are considerably more restrictive.

This seems like a natural fit for the philosophy behind ArtCraft: a modern, user-controlled alternative to a discontinued professional creative tool.

I would personally love to see an **"Encore-like" DiscCraft / AuthorCraft** become part of the ArtCraft family.

Thank you fo…

title: [Bug] Denied task-queue localStorage read prevents the frontend from mounting
author: Jagalite
body:
Rejecting one optional task-queue localStorage read makes the production frontend render a blank screen before account setup. Restoring that read and reloading restores the normal account-creation screen.

## Environment

- Current main `3e5793b6934b51536606720e5d56bcfd1fe7cc2d`, rechecked on 2026-10-07; unchanged from the tested locked production Vite build.
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64, Apple M1; isolated standalone Chrome 154.0.8037.93, Firefox 155.0 and Playwright WebKit 26.6 (not Safari), headless, frontend hosted at a loopback root.
- Standalone production frontend only. No mocked Tauri bridge, test account, provider calls or packaged-WebView qualification.

## Reproduction

1. Before the frontend entry mounts, wrap `Storage.prototype.getItem` to throw `new DOMException("Generated task queue read denial", "SecurityError")` only when the receiver is `localStorage` and the key is `taskQueueLastReadAt`. Delegate every other read to the original implementation.
2. Load the production frontend and wait four seconds after DOM readiness. Inspect the visible page and `#root.childElementCount`; capture uncaught errors and the intercepted key.
3. Disable the fault and reload the same isolated page. Inspect the root and visible screen again.
4. Repeat in a clean context without the fault as a baseline.

## Actual

All three engines reproduce:

- The optional key is read twice; both reads are rejected.
- The React root has zero children and the screen is blank. An uncaught SecurityError is recorded.
- Restoring the single read and reloading gives two root children and the ordinary account-creation UI. Clean no-fault controls reach the same account UI.
- The failure occurs before an authenticated viewer or provider scenario is needed.

## Expected

Treat an unavailable last-read timestamp as absent/default and allow the frontend to mount. An optional task-queue preference should not replace the entire application with a blank screen.

## Relevant code and limits

[`TaskQueue.tsx`]…

title: [Bug / UX] Windows MSI installer appears to crash silently (No UI wizard, no desktop shortcut, instant exit in maintenance mode)
author: lalitmahajn
body:
### Environment
- **App:** PrintCraft
- **Release:** 0.2.1 (Latest stable release)
- **Asset:** `printcraft-0.2.1-windows-x64.msi`
- **OS:** Windows 10 / 11 (x64)

---

### Problem Description
When running `printcraft-0.2.1-windows-x64.msi`, the installer appears to crash or fail silently:
1. **No Setup Wizard:** Running the installer does not display any setup dialog or wizard (no Welcome, Directory selection, or Completion screens). Only a brief Windows Installer progress dialog flashes momentarily.
2. **No Post-Install Launch or Desktop Icon:** Once finished, the app does not automatically launch, and no shortcut is created on the Desktop (only placed in the Start Menu). To users, it seems as if the installer closed without doing anything.
3. **Instant Exit on Re-run (Simulating a Crash):** If a user re-launches the `.msi` (believing the first run failed), the window flashes for less than a second and immediately terminates with no message.

---

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Download `printcraft-0.2.1-windows-x64.msi`.
2. Double-click the `.msi` file to install.
3. Observe that no setup wizard appears, no desktop shortcut is generated, and the app does not launch.
4. Double-click the `.msi` file again.
5. Notice the installer dialog appears for ~0.5 seconds and disappears immediately without any prompt or error.

---

### Expected Behavior
- The installer should provide a standard setup wizard UI (Welcome, Install options, Finish dialog).
- An option or default to create a Desktop shortcut.
- An option or default to launch PrintCraft upon completion.
- If the application is already installed, running the MSI should open a Maintenance Dialog ("Modify / Repair / Remove") rather than executing a silent reconfiguration that immediately closes.

title: Strategic Growth: Capturing the Massive Indian Market with Native Indic language Support
author: Alisowetto
body:
Hi Brandon and the team! I'm a designer from India, and I've been following the ArtCraft suite with a lot of excitement. To be completely honest, the #1 reason I'm looking for an alternative is that I refuse to pay Adobe's massive subscription fees—they are completely out of line with local earnings here. 

Right now, millions of Indian designers and students are forced to use buggy, unsafe, pirated versions of Photoshop and Illustrator because we don't have a choice. We want a clean, legal, lightweight alternative, but there is one massive roadblock keeping us from switching to ArtCraft: lack of native Indic language support (like Bengali, Hindi, etc.).

Because Indic scripts are complex, typing Bengali in the current text engine breaks the letters apart—conjunct clusters fail to merge, and vowel markers (matras) sit on the wrong side. 

If VectorCraft, PhotoCraft, and DesignCraft can integrate a proper complex text-shaping engine (like HarfBuzz), you will instantly solve a problem for millions of Indian creators. A fast, free, Rust-powered tool that flawlessly handles our regional typography would disrupt Adobe's hold on the South Asian market overnight.

title: Proposal: MCP server for agent access (library, generation and 3D Stage)
author: RafaelJaime
body:
## Summary

Expose ArtCraft to AI agents through an MCP server, so that agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex can use the library, generation and above all the **3D Stage** without driving the GUI.

## Why

I'm building promo films with an agent pipeline: the agent writes the shot list, generates stills and clips, and assembles the edit in code. ArtCraft's most valuable feature for that pipeline is the one no other tool offers: blocking a scene in 3D, with consistent locations, character placement and an exact camera, before generating.

Today the only way an agent can reach it is desktop "computer use": screenshots plus mouse clicks. I tried it on a real project:

- It works only as far as typing numbers into the transform panel. Dragging presets into the scene is fragile.
- Every action costs a screenshot round-trip, and the agent takes over the user's screen.
- Scene state can't be read back, so the agent can't verify what it built.

I dropped ArtCraft from that project and generated every shot elsewhere. A small, typed tool surface would have made it the blocking step of the pipeline.

## What already exists

The repo already defines MCP session auth: `POST /v1/mcp/session/create`, plus refresh, revoke, list and delete in `crates/api_clients/artcraft/artcraft_api_defs/src/mcp_sessions/`, and `PlatformType::Mcp`. That suggests a hosted MCP server is planned. This issue is meant to help shape its tool surface and to ask whether the 3D Stage can be part of it.

## Proposed tools

**Library (cloud, uses the MCP session token)**
- `media_list({ type?, uploads_only?, cursor? })`
- `media_upload({ filename, bytes | url })`: uploads as a user file, visible in the library (see #2001 for why the flag matters)
- `media_get({ token })`

**Generation (cloud)**
- `models_list({ kind: image|video|audio|mesh|splat })`, including cost per call
- `generate({ model, prompt, references[], aspect_ratio, duration? })` → job token
- `job_status({ job })`, which returns result me…

title: You are asking for lawsuits
author: CHJ85
body:
You guys need to walk a lot more careful. The phrasing—flaunting **"clean-room reimplementation of Adobe Photoshop/Illustrator"** right there in the repository headers—is essentially waving a red cape in front of a corporate bull.

To a layperson, saying "we rewrote Photoshop from scratch" sounds like a legal safe-harbor keyword. To an intellectual property lawyer, it looks like a neon sign blinking: *"Please look closely at our codebase and how it was made."*

Using the term "clean-room" is a calculated legal defense, but putting it front and center in a repository description while cloning a multi-billion-dollar corporation's product line creates massive vulnerabilities for a few reasons:

### 1. The Paradox of the "Clean-Room" Claim

A true legal clean-room design requires a strict, verifiable firewall:

* Team A analyzes Adobe's software behavior and writes *functional specifications* (what the software should do, without looking at the underlying code).
* Team B (who has never seen Adobe's code *or* reverse-engineered it) writes the actual code based strictly on Team A's specs.

When an individual developer "vibe-codes" an entire application suite using an LLM (like Claude), the clean-room defense gets very murky. LLMs are trained on massive swathes of internet data, documentation, and potentially open-source code repositories that touch file formats, rendering logic, and algorithms. If Adobe’s legal team subpoenas the developer or forces discovery on how the code was generated, proving a pristine, legally bulletproof clean-room process becomes an uphill battle.

### 2. Trademark and Trade Dress Aggression

Even if Adobe can't easily sue over pure functionality or standard UI layouts (since tools like Photopea have danced around this line for years), they don't have to limit themselves to copyright.

* **Trade Dress:** If you replicates Adobe's workflow quirks, or visual arrangement so closely that a consumer could reasonably be confused into thinking it's an o…

title: Custom theme from a file: let the desktop supply ArtCraft's colors
author: NobleDoodle
body:
ArtCraft's colors are already CSS variables (`--st-bg`, `--st-panel`, `--st-fg`, `--background`, `--primary`, … in `frontend/apps/artcraft/app/src/styles/base.css`), switched by the `theme-*` class that `st-theme` selects. That's an ideal shape for desktop theming tools (Omarchy's palette, pywal, base16), but nothing outside the app can reach those variables today, so the only option is picking one of the five built-in themes.

**Proposal**

- A "Custom" theme whose colors come from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ai.artcraft.app/theme.json`, or the shared `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/craft/theme.json` proposed for the Crafting Apps in storytold/photocraft#2120, re-read when the file changes.
- The same shared names (`background`, `surface`, `border`, `text`, `textDim`, `accent`, `accentText`, `danger`, `warning`) mapped onto ArtCraft's variables, so one file themes ArtCraft and the Crafting Apps alike.
- `#rrggbb` values only, applied with `style.setProperty`, never as raw CSS; unknown keys ignored.
- Optionally a "System" choice that follows `prefers-color-scheme` between the light theme and a dark one.

I'm happy to help with a PR if this direction works for you.

title: [Bug] Linux release build: WebKit process crashes on Wayland (DMABUF renderer)
author: BluePhi09
body:
**Environment:** CachyOS (Arch), x86_64, Wayland, webkit2gtk-4.1 2.52.6, ArtCraft 0.42.0 built from source via `script/artcraft/unix_build.sh` (AppImage bundle)

**Problem:** Starting the built AppImage fails immediately:

```
Gdk-Message: Error 71 (Protocol error) dispatching to Wayland display.
ERROR: WebKit encountered an internal error. This is a WebKit bug.
.../WebProcess/Network/WebLoaderStrategy.cpp(738) : void WebKit::WebLoaderStrategy::networkProcessCrashed()
```

**Workaround:** `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 ./ArtCraft_0.42.0_amd64.AppImage` starts normally.

**Cause:** The dev scripts (`unix_dev.sh`/`unix-dev.mjs`, `unix_rust_dev.sh`) already set `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`, but release builds don't, so the crash only shows up outside dev.

title: Performance: startup bundle size and task-queue polling
author: 0X11Dynamic
body:
Notes from a performance pass over the desktop app. The small fixes are in a separate PR; these need a maintainer's call, so I am raising them rather than changing them.

## 1. The entry JS chunk is 6.5 MB

`npx vite build` in `frontend/apps/artcraft` produces:

| Chunk                          | Size      |
|--------------------------------|-----------|
| `index-*.js` (entry)           | 6,502 kB  |
| `index-*.js` (second)          | 1,586 kB  |
| `index-*.js` (contains ammo)   | 422 kB    |
| `opencut_wasm_bg-*.wasm`       | 3,038 kB  |

The entry chunk contains three.js, the Spark splat renderer, Konva, PostHog and zip.js, so they are parsed on every launch even though `MainApp.tsx` lazy-loads its pages. Something on the eager import path (probably a barrel `index.ts` or a shared store) pulls them in. `vite.config.ts` has no `manualChunks`. I have not timed startup, only measured the output size.

## 2. `list_tasks_for_frontend` returns every non-dismissed task, every 5 seconds

`crates/schema/database/sqlite_tasks/src/queries/list_tasks_for_frontend.rs` has no `LIMIT` and filters only on `is_dismissed_by_user`, which has no index. Completed tasks are never auto-dismissed, so the result grows with history. Two components poll it on separate 5s timers (`TopBar/TaskQueue.tsx` and `generation-feed/useDesktopGenerationFeed.ts`) and then discard most rows client-side. Completion and failure events are already pushed over Tauri events, so the interval could be a slow fallback. A fix probably wants a "recent tasks" query plus an index, which means a migration, so I left it alone.

## 3. `useActiveJobs` may be polling for nothing

`MainApp.tsx` mounts `useActiveJobs`, which calls `JobsApi.ListRecentJobs()` on mount and every 2-10s while a job is active, and shows an error toast on failure. I could not find any component that reads the signals it fills (`recentJobs`, `activeJobs`, `completed*` in `signals/activeJobs.ts`). If that is right, the hook and its poller can go. …

### Motivation
With the growing adoption of Windows on ARM PCs (Snapdragon X Elite / X Plus / Copilot+ PCs), native ARM64 support is becoming increasingly important. 

Currently, only the x64 Windows installer is provided in Releases. While the x64 binary can run under Windows 11 emulation (Prism), a native ARM64 build would:
- Deliver significantly better CPU efficiency and lower memory footprint.
- Maximize battery life on portable ARM laptops.
- Take full advantage of native WebView2 and Rust runtime performance without emulation overhead.

### Proposed Solution
Since ArtCraft is built with Tauri and Rust, adding Windows ARM64 support is straightforward via cross-compilation on GitHub Actions (`windows-latest` runner)

title: Feature request: Twint for one-time credit pack purchases
author: HighTecno
body:
## Request

Let users pay for one-time credit packs with Twint (Swiss mobile payments).

## What I found in the code

- `stripe_artcraft_create_credits_pack_checkout_handler.rs` (in `artcraft-services`) builds a `CheckoutSessionMode::Payment` session with a fixed `price_id` per pack and does not set `payment_method_types`. Stripe therefore picks payment methods from the dashboard configuration.
- So Twint may only need enabling in the Stripe dashboard. I can't see the account, so I can't confirm that.
- Stripe supports Twint only for CHF. The packs use fixed price IDs, which look USD-priced in the client (`$10/$25/$50/$100` in `credits-modal.tsx`). Showing Twint probably means CHF prices (or Stripe's multi-currency prices) for the packs.
- The session sets `setup_future_usage: OnSession`. Worth checking that this is compatible with Twint.

## Question

Would you rather enable it in the dashboard with CHF pricing, or have a PR that adds explicit currency handling? I'm happy to help with either.

title: Stylus input broken in all Linux desktop apps and the Launcher (Wayland): cursor moves, clicks don't registe
author: SArneitzUni
body:
Environment:

    Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, GNOME on Wayland
    MSI Prestige 16 AI+ Flip (built-in pen display/digitizer)
    Apps (all latest versions) installed via  ArtCraft Launcher (craft-launcher v0.2.0).

Description:
The stylus cannot be used inside the apps and the main launcher. The pen moves the cursor inside the app window, but clicks/presses do not register at all — no drawing, no UI interaction with the pen. Touch and mouse work normally.

Diagnostics:

-     The app runs as a native Wayland client (does not appear in xlsclients while running).
-     No warnings or errors in terminal output when touching pen to screen.
-     The pen works correctly in other native Wayland apps (Firefox, GNOME Settings) and in Qt apps forced to Wayland (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland krita).
-     The pen works in the WebAssembly/browser version of the app, so canvas input handling works — the issue is specific to the desktop input stack.

Likely cause: On Wayland, stylus events are delivered via the zwp_tablet_v2 protocol, not as wl_pointer events. The desktop app appears to only handle pointer events, so pen motion moves the cursor (compositor-side) but pen-down never reaches the app. Handling tablet-tool events (or synthesizing pointer clicks from pen contact) would fix this. For a drawing-focused tool, full pressure support via the tablet protocol would also be very welcome.

title: [App Request] Visio: a diagramming Craft app (stencils, smart connectors, .vsdx)
author: charles-hood
body:
## The gap

Of the Office family, Word, Excel and PowerPoint now have Craft apps. Visio does not, and it is the one Microsoft sells separately: Visio Plan 1 and Plan 2 are their own subscriptions on top of Microsoft 365, with the desktop app only on Plan 2. The people who need it (network and datacenter engineers, systems architects, process and compliance teams, anyone drawing an org chart or a floor plan) tend to be exactly the people who were told "we don't pay for Visio here" and ended up drawing boxes in PowerPoint instead.

The alternatives each miss something. draw.io is free and good but is a web app in an Electron shell, with no real stencil ecosystem and weak .vsdx fidelity. Lucidchart is SaaS with a per-seat subscription. yEd is Java and dated. LibreOffice Draw is a page layout tool, not a diagrammer. None of them is a native, offline, cross-platform desktop app that opens the .vsdx files vendors ship.

## What a DiagramCraft would need

In rough priority order, from someone who draws storage and network topologies for a living:

1. **Stencils (masters) and the shape sheet.** Visio's whole value is a shape that knows what it is: a switch master with named connection points, a text field bound to a property, a resize that keeps the port layout. Vendor stencil packs (Cisco, Dell, HPE, Brocade, Juniper, AWS, Azure) are .vssx files; reading those is the single biggest compatibility win.
2. **Smart connectors.** Glue to connection points, dynamic glue to a shape's edge, orthogonal routing with line jumps, reroute on move, arrowheads and line ends per connector, connector text that stays with the line.
3. **Pages, layers, containers and lists.** Multi-page documents with background pages, layers with visibility and lock, container shapes that own what is inside them.
4. **.vsdx read and write.** It is OPC plus XML, like .pptx, so the `deckcraft` OPC and DrawingML code is a head start. .vsdm (macro) can be read and the macros dropped.
5. **Export.** PNG, SVG, PD…

title: [App Request] CommitCraft – a visual Git client for creatives (GitHub Desktop Plus alternative)
author: matbrgz
body:
[![Status: Proposed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-proposed-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Type: App Request](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-app_request-blueviolet.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Ecosystem: Artcraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-artcraft-8A2BE2.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-DEA584.svg?style=flat-square&logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org)

## ELI5
Git is a time machine for files. Coders use it every day, but for artists it is scary and it shows images as "binary file changed".
CommitCraft would be a simple Git app (like GitHub Desktop Plus) that **understands art files**.

## What it does
- Save points (commits) with a thumbnail of each image, video or 3D file
- Visual diff: old vs new side by side (A/B slider, onion skin)
- Branches shown as "variations" (cyberpunk / medieval / corporate)
- Fork a creation from the community and keep the whole history
- Git LFS built in, so big files just work

## Why
- Artists lose track of "how did I make this?"
- No good open-source Git client shows creative diffs
- First step toward a shared project history across all Craft apps

title: [App Request] An Orca alternative – parallel AI agents and worktrees with Git LFS for big assets
author: matbrgz
body:
[![Status: Proposed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-proposed-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Type: App Request](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-app_request-blueviolet.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Ecosystem: Artcraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-artcraft-8A2BE2.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-DEA584.svg?style=flat-square&logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org)

Orca lets you run many AI helpers at once, each in its own copy of the project (a Git worktree), so they don't step on each other.
This app would do the same for creative projects, where files are huge (video, 3D, PSD), using Git LFS.

## What it does
- Spawn several agents, each in its own worktree/branch
- Each agent tries a different idea; you compare and pick the best

title: [Feature Request] .craft – an open project format shared by all Craft apps
author: matbrgz
body:
[![Status: Proposed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-proposed-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Type: Feature Request](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-feature_request-brightgreen.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Ecosystem: Artcraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-artcraft-8A2BE2.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-DEA584.svg?style=flat-square&logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org)

## ELI5
Today a finished image is just a JPG. You lose the recipe: the prompt, the model, the seed, the masks, the camera.
A `.craft` file is a box that keeps the result **and** every step that made it, so you (or anyone) can open it and redo or change any step.

```text
scene.craft
├── manifest.json
├── assets/
├── prompts/
├── generations/   (model, version, seed, params)
├── timeline/
└── history/       (every step as a commit)
```

## Motivation
- Answer "how did I make this?" forever
- Open and documented: any app, any model, no lock-in
- Git-friendly, so it works with versioning, branches and forks
- Swap the model on one step (FLUX → GPT Image → local) and rerun
- One project model for PhotoCraft, FilmCraft, SoundCraft, etc. instead of loose files

title: [App Request] NoteCraft – a local-first Notion/Obsidian alternative
author: matbrgz
body:
[![Status: Proposed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-proposed-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Type: App Request](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-app_request-blueviolet.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Ecosystem: Artcraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-artcraft-8A2BE2.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-DEA584.svg?style=flat-square&logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org)

## ELI5
A notebook for ideas, docs, moodboards and tasks. Everything lives as files on your computer, not locked in someone's cloud.

## Motivation
- Your knowledge should outlive any company
- Notion is closed and cloud-only; Obsidian is closed source
- Markdown files + Git = history, sync and backup you control
- Natural home for briefs, scripts and moodboards that feed other Craft apps
- Agents can read and write notes via CLI/MCP

title: [App Request] VaultCraft – an open media library (Google Photos / Eagle alternative)
author: matbrgz
body:

## ELI5
One place to keep all your images, videos, 3D files and generations, searchable by what's in them, stored where **you** choose.

## Motivation
- Billions of personal photos live in a few big clouds
- Local AI search ("red car at sunset") without uploading anything
- Keeps provenance and license info for each asset (who made it, which model, can I use it?)
- Helps fight fake content: you can prove where a file came from
- Shared asset pool for every Craft app and every `.craft` project

title: [App Request] KeyCraft – a local-first password & passkey manager (1Password alternative)
author: matbrgz
body:
[![Status: Proposed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-proposed-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Type: App Request](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-app_request-blueviolet.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Ecosystem: Artcraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-artcraft-8A2BE2.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-DEA584.svg?style=flat-square&logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org)

## ELI5
A safe for all your passwords, passkeys and API keys. It locks with one master key and fills logins for you.

## Motivation
- 1Password is closed source; Bitwarden is open but built around a server
- Local-first vault (encrypted file you own), optional sync
- Perfect home for **BYOK model API keys** (OpenAI, fal, Replicate…) used by every Craft app, instead of plain-text config
- Passkeys help kill phishing and password reuse on the internet
- Agents can request a key via CLI/MCP without ever seeing the whole vault

title: [App Request] CADCraft – 3D CAD, CAM & mechanical design (Autodesk Fusion 360 alternative)
author: mateowoetam
body:
**Problem / Context**
Artists, makers, and hardware designers using the Craft ecosystem currently lack an integrated parametric 3D CAD and CAM workspace for mechanical design, assembly modeling, and manufacturing preparation, forcing them to jump to proprietary cloud-locked tools like Autodesk Fusion 360.

**Proposed Solution**
Introduce **CADCraft**, a focused app within the Craft ecosystem tailored for precise 3D parametric modeling, mechanical assemblies, sheet metal design, and CAM toolpath generation, keeping workflow state locally inside `.craft` project files.

**Key Features**
* **Parametric Sketching & Modeling:** Dimension-driven 2D sketches mapped to robust 3D features, lofts, sweeps, and fillets.
* **Assembly Constraints:** Component mating, joints, and motion links to test mechanical mechanisms.
* **CAM & Toolpaths:** Basic 2.5axis and 3axis CNC milling simulations, G-code generation, and 3D printing preparation.
* **Blender & Mesh Bridge:** Clean conversion tools to transition precise CAD NURBS/BREP data into organic meshes for texture and render apps.

title: [App Request] MailCraft – a lightweight, local-first email app (Outlook alternative)
author: matbrgz
body:
[![Status: Proposed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-proposed-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Type: App Request](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-app_request-blueviolet.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Ecosystem: Artcraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-artcraft-8A2BE2.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-DEA584.svg?style=flat-square&logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org)

## ELI5
A small, fast email app for creators: read and send mail, see attachments as previews, and drag an image straight into PhotoCraft or a `.craft` project. Not a full Outlook clone — just the part people use every day.

Builds on the idea in storytold/artcraft-services#80, scoped down to a **lightweight v1**.

## v1 scope
- IMAP/SMTP and JMAP, multiple accounts, unified inbox
- Local-first: mail cached on disk, fast offline search
- Media-aware: image/video/PDF previews, "Open in Craft app"
- Credentials stored locally (KeyCraft #2137 later)
- Later: calendar/contacts (CalDAV/CardDAV), Exchange, PST import

## Self-hosted option (available today)
- [Stalwart](https://github.com/stalwartlabs/stalwart) (AGPL-3.0 / commercial): all-in-one mail server in Rust (JMAP, IMAP, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV). Users can run their own server and point MailCraft at it.
- [Thunderbird for Android](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android) (Apache-2.0): mature open mail client, a reference for IMAP handling.

## Motivation
- Email is still the open backbone of the internet; clients are getting closed and cloud-relayed
- Rust + JMAP fits the Craft apps' stack
- Small scope ships faster than a full Outlook replacement

title: [App Request] MapCraft – open GIS and map design (ArcGIS alternative, publishes to GeoServer)
author: matbrgz
body:
[![Status: Proposed](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-proposed-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Type: App Request](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-app_request-blueviolet.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Ecosystem: Artcraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/ecosystem-artcraft-8A2BE2.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft) [![Language: Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/language-Rust-DEA584.svg?style=flat-square&logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org)

## ELI5
A map maker. Load places, roads, rivers or your own data, style them beautifully, and export a map for print, the web or a 3D scene. Like ArcGIS, but open and on your computer.

## What it does
- Open common geo data: GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoTIFF, KML, PMTiles
- Style maps visually (colors, labels, icons) and export to print/PDF, SVG or web tiles
- Terrain from elevation data → 3D scenes in ArtCraft ("put my scene in the real Alps")
- Publish a map as a web page or via standard OGC services (WMS/WFS)
- Built in Rust on georust/GDAL, with MapLibre for interactive maps

## Self-hosted option (available today)
- [GeoServer](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver) (GPL-2.0): the standard open server to publish maps and geo data (WMS, WFS, WMTS). Users can self-host it today and MapCraft can publish to it.
- [QGIS](https://github.com/qgis/QGIS) (GPL-2.0): mature open desktop GIS, a reference for features and formats.
- [MapLibre](https://github.com/maplibre/maplibre-gl-js) and [PMTiles](https://github.com/protomaps/PMTiles) (BSD-3): open web maps and single-file tiles, easy to embed.

## Motivation
- ArcGIS is expensive and closed; cities, NGOs and schools struggle to pay for it
- QGIS is powerful but hard for designers; there is no "beautiful maps" tool for creatives
- Maps feed infographics, film locations, games and architecture (BIMCraft #2157)
- Open data + open formats = maps anyone can check and reuse

## ELI5
A shared toolbox for every Craft app. Save a color, font, brush, logo or 3D material once, and it shows up in PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, FilmCraft, DeckCraft… Change it in one place, it updates everywhere.

## What goes in a library
- Colors and palettes (ASE, GPL), gradients
- Fonts (links to [craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts))
- Brushes (ABR), LUTs (CUBE), presets, filters
- Stencils and shapes (Visio `.vssx`, see #2121), icons, logos
- Materials (MaterialX), 3D models (glTF/USD), HDRIs

## How it works
- A library is just a folder with a `library.json` manifest + files → readable, Git-friendly, no lock-in
- **Local first**; share by syncing the folder (Git, DriveCraft #2139, any cloud) or publishing to CraftHub (#2151)
- Team/brand libraries: a company shares one "Brand Kit" library with all designers
- Each item keeps license and source (who made it, can I use it commercially?)
- Imports Adobe CC Libraries exports, Procreate brushes, Figma styles where possible

## Motivation
- Today each app has its own presets; switching apps means redoing them

- Brand consistency for teams without a subscription
- The `.craft` format (#2131) can reference library items instead of copying them

## ELI5
People don't choose apps, they double-click files. If ArtCraft opens the files people already have, they switch. And instead of one app per idea, group the ideas into **a few apps with modes** (like Blender has modes, not 10 apps).

This also answers #1999 (too many apps): fewer, stronger apps.

## What the world actually uses (data)
- **Web images:** PNG on 76.5% of websites, JPEG 70.7%, SVG 67.0%, WebP 20.8%, GIF 14.2%, AVIF 1.5% ([W3Techs, Jul 2026](https://w3techs.com/technologies/overview/image_format)). JPEG is slowly falling, SVG/WebP/AVIF rising ([Web Almanac 2024](https://almanac.httparchive.org/en/2024/media)).

- **Documents:** PDF is the universal document; a widely quoted estimate is ~2.5 trillion PDFs ([PDF Association](https://www.pdfa.org/PDF-in-2016-broader-deeper-richer/)).

title: [Proposal] Make ArtCraft apps work together intelligently — especially for AI agents
author: angel1411337-del
body:
ArtCraft is building an impressive collection of applications, but I think there's an opportunity to make the whole suite much more powerful than the individual apps.

Consider a simple example.

I'm working on a marketing campaign. I've created a logo in VectorCraft, animations in EffectCraft, videos in FilmCraft, and a presentation in DeckCraft.

The client asks me to change the logo.

**Ideally, ArtCraft should know everywhere that logo is used.** It should identify which projects will update automatically, which need to be re-rendered, and which contain copies that need manual attention.

Now imagine giving an AI agent the instruction:

> We've changed the branding. Update everything affected and make sure it's consistent.

The agent could inspect the relationships between projects, figure out what needs changing, use each application's existing CLI/MCP tools, and check the results.

This goes beyond linking files or running predefined automation sequences. It would let agents understand how work across different applications fits together.

## How this relates to existing proposals

I noticed several discussions already pointing in this direction:

- [Shared `.craft` projects](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/issues/2131)
- [Reusable Craft Recipes](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/issues/2132)
- [AutoCraft automation](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/issues/2144)
- [FilmCraft ↔ EffectCraft integration](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1024)

I think these could benefit from a common foundation that tracks **what projects contain, how their contents are related, and what is affected when something changes.**

Each application would remain independent and responsible for its own files. The shared system would help applications and AI agents understand the bigger picture.

## Overview

Add support for Loupedeck control surfaces (and the new Logitech MX Creative Console) to **FilmCraft**, **LightCraft**, and **PhotoCraft**.

### Hardware Details

- **Loupedeck line**: Live, Live S, CT, and Razer Stream Controller (discontinued March 2025)
- **Current**: Logitech MX Creative Console (Oct 2024 replacement)
- **Integration**: Other creative apps (Premiere, Photoshop, Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, OBS) use the **Logi Actions SDK** to write plugins

## Current State ✅

All three apps already have loopback JSON control channels that can execute any engine/UI command:

- **FilmCraft**: `--control <port>` (~975 commands including timeline ops, playback)
- **LightCraft**: `--control 7980` (already lists control surfaces as 🟡 partial in `docs/hardware-parity.md`)
- **PhotoCraft**: `--control` + auth token

No driver code needed in the apps themselves.

## Recommended Approach: Logi Actions SDK Plugin

**Effort**: ~1-2 weeks per app  
**Coverage**: Loupedeck, Razer Stream Controller, and MX Creative Console

1. Write a **C# or Node.js plugin** using Logitech's official SDK
2. Plugin communicates with the existing control channels via loopback
3. Lives in a **separate repo** (not pure Rust, can't go in ArtCraft repos per AGENTS.md
4. Users install both the plugin and the apps

### Benefits
- No ArtCraft code changes to start
- Vendor handles device screens, profiles, and UI
- Supports current and future Logitech hardware
- Follows the same pattern as Premiere/Lightroom/DaVinci plugins

title: Bug: Selecting Text Within a Single PDF Table Cell Selects the Entire Row
author: Yosef-kelfin
body: ## Description When selecting text inside a table in a PDF document using PDFCraft in ArcCraft, the text selection behaves incorrectly. Even when the cursor is positioned and dragged entirely within a single table cell, the application selects the entire row instead of only the text inside the intended cell. This behavior makes it difficult to select, copy, or work with specific text within PDF tables. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a PDF document containing a table in ArcCraft. 2. Navigate to a table with multiple rows and columns. 3. Place the text selection cursor inside a specific cell. 4. Click and drag to select only a portion of the text within that cell. 5. Observe the resulting text selection. ## Expected Behavior Only the text within the selected cell should be highlighted, according to the cursor position and selection boundaries. The selection should remain limited to the text explicitly selected by the user. ## Actual Behavior The application selects the entire table row instead of the intended text within a single cell, even when the cursor remains within the boundaries of that cell. ## Impact - Prevents precise text selection within PDF tables. - Makes copying individual cell contents difficult or inconvenient. - Disrupts the expected text-selection experience when working with structured PDF documents. ## Environment - **Application:** ArcCraft - **Component:** PDFCraft - **Document type:** PDF containing tables - **Operating system:** Not specified - **Application version:** Not specified ## Additional Information The issue appears to be related to text-selection behavior within table structures. The selection boundaries do not appear to respect the intended text range within an individual cell. title: Have you considered using REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) as a development tool?
author: JaredTweed
body:
Hi! I was wondering whether the ArtCraft team is already using, or has considered using, "REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)" (https://github.com/morluto/rea) during development.

REA is an open-source MCP toolkit that allows AI coding agents to investigate native applications, JavaScript/Electron apps, websites, and runtime behavior.

It seems like it could be useful for ArtCraft when researching how established creative tools implement particular features, such as:

- 2D compositing and image-editing behavior
- 3D scene manipulation and camera controls
- Image/video editing workflows and export behavior
- Complex interactions and edge cases that aren't well documented

It could potentially accelerate development by helping AI agents understand existing implementations and identify useful behavior to reproduce, while respecting licensing and clean-room development practices.

A couple of questions:

1. Is the team already using REA or a similar application-analysis tool?
2. If not, would it be worth experimenting with REA on a particular workflow to see whether it could improve development efficiency?

I'm suggesting it as an optional development tool rather than something that necessarily needs to be integrated into ArtCraft itself.

Thanks for considering it!

title: PDF export in PrintCraft/PDFCraft not working well
author: paddydun
body:
Tried exporting a few PDFs to Word (using Mac OS 15.7.4) and formatting was generally a mess. 

1. Tried a newsletter with quite a few 2 column pages - the Word version has only one column. Text was often in the wrong places (text in the right column would appear before the text in the left column), photos missing, paragraph breaks missing, footers not in footer section (mixed into main body) - generally not usable. 
2. I tried converting a PDF to Word that was almost entirely a large table (over 5 pages, with about 5 columns) and it completely broke. It was a list of names, address, phone numbers, email addresses... Titles for columns were just text - in a vertical list. First two columns generally worked, but after that, it was very broken. Text for the third column was mostly not in the column at all, but at the bottom of each page. Text for 4th column was *mostly* where it belonged except in some instances where it stretched over 2 or 3 columns. 

Note: I tried converting both of these documents in Adobe Acrobat and the newsletter was better but definitely full of issues as well (it did manage the 2 column layout for the most part, but made a mess of the fonts etc.) Acrobat converted the table doc very well - no errors and looked exactly like the PDF.

title: [Feature] Self-hosted ArtCraft cloud: file sync, personal drive, web app builds, and one-command server deployment
author: achose369
body:
The Craft suite already has two halves of a Creative Cloud alternative: great native desktop apps with the launcher as the install hub, and artcraft-services with a self-hostable backend (docker-compose in build/selfhost). What's missing is the connective tissue that makes it feel like one product: your files available everywhere, the apps usable from a browser, and a server you can actually deploy without compiling Rust for an hour. This request bundles four related features that together would make ArtCraft a genuine self-hosted Creative Cloud replacement.

1. Web builds of the Craft apps, officially distributed and self-hostable

    The apps are advertised as "Web-native" and community projects like CraftHub already serve web builds — make this official.
    Publish the WASM web builds of each Craft app as release artifacts alongside the desktop builds, the way the launcher already ships per-platform binaries.
    Document how to host them: static files + a pointer at a backend URL, so anyone can serve the apps from their own domain or local network.
    Ideally the launcher's web build graduates from "catalog site" to actually launching/opening the web builds of the apps, so the browser experience mirrors the desktop launcher.

2. ArtCraft Drive: file sync across devices

    A sync client (or sync built into the launcher) that keeps a local folder in sync with the user's cloud storage, Dropbox-style: create/edit on desktop, pick up on laptop or in the web app.
    Desktop apps should be able to open and save directly against synced projects, not just local files, so a PhotoCraft project started on one machine opens on another.
    Basics expected of any sync system: delta/block-level sync for large media files, pause/resume, selective sync per folder, bandwidth limits, and clear conflict resolution (keep both, never silently overwrite).
    Offline-first: apps keep working with local copies when the server is unreachable and reconcile on reconnect.

title: [Feature Request] Add custom installation directory picker with automatic updates to Craft Apps Manager
author: SharabhaDesign
body:
Hello ArtCraft team, Thank you for these great apps.

Currently, the ArtCraft Launcher automatically installs all suite applications (PhotoCraft, VectorCraft, FilmCraft, etc.) directly into the AppData\Local path on the C: drive without prompting the user. For users with limited space on their primary SSD, forcing large applications and heavy future updates onto the C: drive causes severe storage issues.

I would like to see a global setting within the launcher settings (or a prompt during individual app installations) that allows users to pick a custom destination directory (e.g., D:\CreativeApps). Future automatic updates should also respect this custom path.

I have looked into switching the launcher's release format to "Portable ZIP," but this removes the seamless nature of automatic background updates. I have also tried setting up directory junctions (mklink /J), but a native setting inside the launcher would provide a much smoother, safer user experience for the community.

title: [Idea] Consolidate overlapping apps, i.e PhotoCraft and LightCraft
author: CHJ85
body:
Adobe split Photoshop and Lightroom into two separate applications back in the day not because it made logical sense for a workflow, but because of legacy codebases, corporate acquisitions, and a desire to charge users for two separate licenses (or force them into higher photography bundle tiers).

In practice, a creator constantly jumps back and forth between editing a photo's tone/color and doing deep edits or retouching. Keeping them separate forces you to deal with file round-tripping, export/import loops, or clunky sync databases.

Because ArtCraft isn't handcuffed to 30 years of legacy C++ technical debt or a corporate sales model that depends on upselling multiple tiers, they don't have to perpetuate Adobe's arbitrary walls. Merging `Photocraft` and `Lightcraft` into a single, unified, snappy workspace—where non-destructive raw grading and pixel-level painting live side-by-side seamlessly—would actually create something *better* than the industry standard, rather than just cloning it.

Streamlining the suite by consolidating redundant or artificially divided apps would make the whole ecosystem punch way above its weight class.

Then there's the **"fair use and transformative innovation"** argument.
If Adobe ever tried to claim that ArtCraft was engaging in unlawful market confusion or slavish copying, the ArtCraft team could flip the script entirely:

title: SQLite startup deletes task storage after any connection or migration error
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- rust-audit:d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373:db-reset -->
## Assessment

**Severity:** High — conditional loss of local task history. **Confidence:** High in the source behavior; runtime/security preconditions are qualified below.

Found during an AI-assisted, read-only Rust audit of upstream main at [d4e4ac6](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/commit/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373). No application exploits, authenticated provider requests, or destructive tests were performed. Rust/native runtime tests were not available; proposed tests below are not claimed as executed.

## Source evidence and root cause

- [`crates/schema/database/sqlite_tasks/src/connection.rs:14–61`](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/blob/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373/crates/schema/database/sqlite_tasks/src/connection.rs#L14-L61)

`connect_and_migrate()` catches every error from `run_migrations()`, then calls `std::fs::remove_file(&database_file)` and retries. `run_migrations()` includes both opening the pool and running migrations; there is no error classification or backup.

## Trigger and realistic impact

A recoverable connection/locking or migration-checksum error can erase pending-job tracking and completion metadata when deletion succeeds. The database is intentionally described as ephemeral, but the reset applies more broadly than incompatible schemas. On Windows, outstanding handles may prevent deletion and leave startup failing instead.

## Recommended remediation

Preserve the original database on ordinary errors. Classify errors; close connections explicitly before any recovery. Quarantine/back up genuinely incompatible storage rather than unlinking it automatically; account for WAL sidecars and other app instances.

## Suggested regression tests

- Inject connection, lock and migration-checksum failures against disposable databases and assert rows survive.
- Separately test an explicitly approved reset path on Unix and Windows.
- Verify retry/…

title: macOS release diagnostics may emit unencrypted signing-key material
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- rust-audit:d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373:signing-diagnostics -->
## Assessment

**Severity:** High potential impact; historical key exposure NOT established. **Confidence:** High in the source behavior; runtime/security preconditions are qualified below.

Found during an AI-assisted, read-only Rust audit of upstream main at [d4e4ac6](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/commit/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373). No application exploits, authenticated provider requests, or destructive tests were performed. Rust/native runtime tests were not available; proposed tests below are not claimed as executed.

## Source evidence and root cause

- [`.github/workflows/artcraft-macos-publish.yml:98–114`](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/blob/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373/.github/workflows/artcraft-macos-publish.yml#L98-L114)

The workflow runs `openssl pkcs12 ... -info -nodes 2>&1 | head -20`. `-nodes` permits unencrypted private-key output; `head` limits lines but does not filter secrets. Whether key bytes reach the retained output depends on archive ordering. The original encoded secret being masked does not guarantee transformed PEM output is masked.

## Trigger and realistic impact

A signing archive whose key output falls in those lines can disclose signing material to workflow-log readers. No actual certificate, private key or historical log was inspected, and no signing workflow was run. This is a source-confirmed unsafe diagnostic, not a claim of an observed compromise.

## Recommended remediation

Remove diagnostics capable of emitting keys. Use certificate-only `-nokeys` inspection, least-privilege keychain access and unconditional cleanup. Review past logs through an authorized private process; rotate signing material if exposure is confirmed.

## Suggested regression tests

Run the diagnostic code with dummy signing material in an isolated environment; assert neither PEM private-key blocks nor key bytes can enter logs. Never te…

title: artcraft-native: animated preview limits are applied after all frames are decoded
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- rust-audit:d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373:animation-budget -->
## Assessment

**Severity:** High potential availability impact — excessive memory use/OOM. **Confidence:** High in the source behavior; runtime/security preconditions are qualified below.

Found during an AI-assisted, read-only Rust audit of upstream main at [d4e4ac6](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/commit/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373). No application exploits, authenticated provider requests, or destructive tests were performed. Rust/native runtime tests were not available; proposed tests below are not claimed as executed.

## Source evidence and root cause

- [`artcraft-native/src/backend/media_cache.rs:208–238`](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/blob/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373/artcraft-native/src/backend/media_cache.rs#L208-L238)
- [`artcraft-native/src/feed/grid.rs:301–307`](https://github.com/storytold/artcraft/blob/d4e4ac69bbd93d237eaf5d0260bc6a5ff3a5e373/artcraft-native/src/feed/grid.rs#L301-L307)

GIF and WebP paths call `into_frames().collect_frames()` before computing the sampling step and resizing retained frames. Thus the 48-frame/320-pixel preview limits do not bound peak allocations. The pinned image 0.25.6 collector simply collects all returned frames; no aggregate retained-frame budget is provided: https://github.com/image-rs/image/blob/v0.25.6/src/animation.rs#L19-L46 . GIF/WebP iterators return full-canvas image buffers.

## Trigger and realistic impact

An animation with many large frames can exhaust memory when its preview is displayed, including autoplay. For scale, 1,000 full-HD RGBA frames represent about 8.3 GB of pixel buffers before overhead. No crafted media was generated or executed; this is a source-level allocation finding, not a reproduced crash.

## Recommended remediation

The updater truncates with `if s.len() > 255 { &s[..255] } else { s }`. Rust string slicing panics when byte 255 is not a UTF-8 boundary. Remote failure messages are passed directly to this updater.

A long message with a multibyte character crossing byte 255 panics before the database update, potentially terminating the spawned polling task and stopping future status updates. Whole-process termination is not established.

The SQLite column is unrestricted TEXT, so remove truncation if unnecessary; otherwise choose an explicit byte/character limit and truncate only at UTF-8 boundaries.

**Severity:** Medium. **Confidence:** High in source behavior; external effects are qualified below.

Recover provider completion before applying age policy; persist execution versus transfer phase and distinguish offline time from failed execution. Classify FAL permanent errors versus retryable failures and add bounded backoff/retry policy with visible recovery.

title: Refactoring suggestions: a few very large, high-complexity functions and no test CI
author: shiziguode-tech
body:
Hi, thanks for building ArtCraft! I ran a quick static analysis (lizard + ripgrep) on a shallow clone of `main` and noticed a few hotspots that might be worth refactoring for maintainability:

1. `frontend/libs/components/modal/src/lib/modal.tsx:164`: `DragHandle` is about 866 lines with a cyclomatic complexity of 189. Splitting the drag logic into hooks or smaller components could make it much easier to test and review.
2. `gallery-modal.tsx:1063`: an anonymous function of about 1177 lines (CCN 154), in a file of 3771 lines.
3. `video_generation_request.rs:371`: `send_request` has a CCN of 138; splitting it per provider or request type might help.
4. The codebase has 567 TODO/FIXME/HACK markers. Triaging them into issues could help contributors find work.
5. `.github/workflows` currently only has the macOS and Windows release workflows. A test/lint workflow (`cargo test`, `cargo clippy`, frontend type checks) on PRs would catch regressions earlier.

Overall averages look healthy, so this is mostly about a handful of hotspots. Happy to help if any of this is useful!

title: [Feature Request] Unified, context-sensitive grid hotkeys with nested menus and click-to-map across all Craft apps (inspired by StarCraft II "Grid" hotkeys)
author: vinnichase
body:
> *In the name of the -Craft name ancestor: StarCraft II.* 🫡

## Summary
Introduce an optional, position-based "grid" hotkey layout that works the same way in every ArtCraft app — modeled after the Grid hotkey preset in StarCraft II. The grid adapts to the current selection (like the command card for selected units), supports nested sub-grids so that sequences of keys ("key melodies", à la Vim) can reach a practically unlimited number of actions, and offers a mapping mode where users assign functions to grid cells simply by clicking them in the UI.

## How SC2 grid hotkeys work
- The command card is a 5×3 grid of buttons.
- Each grid cell is bound to a fixed key by **position**, not by mnemonic:
  Q W E R T
  A S D F G
  Z X C V B
- Whatever command sits in the top-left cell is always `Q`, regardless of its name. The left hand stays on the home row, and muscle memory carries over between units.
- The command card always shows the commands of the **currently selected units**.

## Proposal
1. Every app/tool context exposes its main actions as a visible grid panel (5×3).
2. Each cell maps to the corresponding key in the layout above.
3. A dedicated key (e.g. `Esc`) always means "back / cancel / up one level".
4. Common actions sit in the **same cell in every app** (e.g. select, move, delete, undo, export), so switching between apps doesn't require relearning.
5. Hotkey labels are shown on the grid buttons, which makes the system self-documenting for new users.
6. Offered as a preset alongside the current/classic shortcuts, not as a forced replacement.

## Context-sensitive grid (selection = "selected units")
Just like the SC2 command card changes with the selected units, the grid adapts to whatever is currently selected:

- **Text selected** → formatting, styles, alignment, lists, links, …
- **Clip(s) selected** (video/audio timeline) → cut, trim, split, speed, fades, effects, …
- **Canvas / image area selected** → crop, fill, transform, filters, layers, …
- **Nothing …

title: Lottie-like animation support needed (open-source alternative to paid tools)
author: Adhishtanaka
body:
## Summary

ArtCraft needs a Lottie-like vector animation feature: lightweight, scalable, JSON-based animations that can be authored, previewed and exported inside the app.

## Motivation

Today the usual route for this kind of animation is a paid tool or service (for example After Effects with Bodymovin, or the paid tiers of LottieFiles). An open-source option built into ArtCraft would let artists, designers and filmmakers create and export these animations without a paid subscription.

## Proposal

- Build an open-source Lottie-compatible animation layer instead of depending on a paid product.
- Import and play existing Lottie (`.json` / `.lottie`) files.
- Do basic authoring: keyframes, shapes, paths, transforms and easing.
- Export to the Lottie JSON format so the output works with the existing players (web, iOS, Android).

## Possible open-source building blocks

- [lottie-web](https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-web) (MIT) for playback and rendering
- [ThorVG](https://github.com/thorvg/thorvg) (MIT) for a lightweight vector and Lottie renderer
- [Skottie / Skia](https://skia.org/docs/user/modules/skottie/) (BSD) for native Lottie rendering
- [rlottie](https://github.com/Samsung/rlottie) (MIT) for native playback

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Users can import and preview Lottie animations
- [ ] Users can create or edit simple vector animations
- [ ] Users can export valid Lottie JSON
- [ ] No paid or proprietary dependency is required

title: Suggestion: a read-only Discord feedback bot that links requests to each app's GitHub issues
author: PhywithAA
body:
### Idea

Add a **read-only feedback bot** to the ArtCraft Discord that collects feature requests and bug reports from each app's channels (DeckCraft, WordCraft, PdfCraft, FilmCraft, PhotoCraft, …) and links them to that app's GitHub issues.

### Why

A lot of useful feedback is posted on Discord, but it scrolls away, gets repeated, and often never reaches the repository where the work is tracked. Meanwhile each repo already keeps careful gap lists (`docs/gaps.md`, `docs/parity-checklist.md`) that Discord users can't easily see. A bot could connect the two:

- Users find out a request is already known, and where to follow it.
- Maintainers see how many people ask for something (useful for prioritising), without reading every channel.
- Fewer duplicate issues, because requests are matched to existing ones first.

### What it could do

1. **Collect:** read messages in the feedback and bug channels of each app (needs the Message Content intent, only in the channels the team chooses).
2. **Group and match:** cluster similar requests, and search that app's open issues for a match.
3. **Report back:**
   - In Discord, reply with a link when a match exists ("Tracked in storytold/deckcraft#148").
   - On GitHub, add a short tally comment ("+3 requests on Discord this week") instead of opening duplicates.
   - Post a weekly digest of new, unmatched requests for a maintainer to triage, and open an issue only once someone approves it.
4. **Privacy:** read only, opt-in channels, no quoting of usernames on GitHub unless the user agrees, and a command to opt out.

### Example from real use

I'm a physics teacher testing DeckCraft, WordCraft and FilmCraft with real class material, and I've filed issues such as storytold/deckcraft#362, storytold/wordcraft#1530 and storytold/wordcraft#1910. Requests like these (equations in decks, bright pen colours for dark slides, SVG pictures) also come up on Discord. A bot would let the whole community's requests reach the right repo with the sa…

title: Feature request: multi-language support (i18n) with drop-in translation files
author: Willemsel
body:
Summary
I’d like to use the ArtCraft apps in Dutch, and I’m willing to contribute the translation. Right now all UI text is hard-coded in English, so there’s no way to add other languages.

**Proposed design**

Built on a standard i18n library (e.g. react-i18next), which loads the JSON files and handles the fallback to English.
A translations/ folder with one JSON file per language.
The file name is the language name, written in that language: English.json, Nederlands.json, Deutsch.json, Français.json, etc.
On startup the app scans the folder and fills the Language dropdown (Settings → Appearance) with the file names. No list of languages is hard-coded.
Adding or improving a language is just adding or editing a JSON file. No code changes and no new release needed.
Missing keys fall back to English.json, so an incomplete translation never breaks the app.
The chosen language is saved and applies immediately. It is independent of the system language, because users don’t always want the app in their OS language.

**Sharing translations**

Users can import/upload a translation file in the app, and it appears in the dropdown right away.
Uploaded translations can be shared, so others can use them immediately without waiting for an update.
All submitted translation files are bundled with each new release, so every user gets all available languages automatically.
Users can add their own translations by placing a JSON file in the translations folder (admin rights may be needed).
Note: a translation that a user makes but doesn’t share could be overwritten by an update. This is an edge case, and sharing translations avoids it.

Applies to all apps
The same folder and the same switch can be used for every ArtCraft app and component.

Proven approach
I use exactly this setup in my own app (Sheet Optimizer), with five languages, and it works well.

Contribution
I’m happy to provide Nederlands.json and help with the implementation. Are you open to this approach?

title: Tauri desktop: isolate remote analytics scripts and restrict local-file asset scope
author: neumdan
body:
## Problem and impact

The Tauri desktop main page combines remote analytics script execution with broadly scoped local-file access. If an allowed script or another main-page JavaScript source is compromised, that code inherits the page's ability to read user-accessible local files, including plaintext provider credentials. This is a high-impact post-compromise boundary weakness; no independent drive-by entry point, provider compromise, or RCE is claimed.

## Verified release and method

title: Subject: Idea for ArtCraft: Camtasia's ergonomics for quick and simple video editing
author: letutorien13
body:
Hi Brandon,

Congratulations on the amazing work you've done on the ArtCraft suite!

For a long time now, I've been trying to run a video editing software I know very well on Linux, without success. That software is Camtasia.

I don't know if you're familiar with it, but for quick and simple videos, its ergonomics are unmatched compared to heavy pro editors like Premiere Pro (or FilmCraft):
1. **Interactive Canvas:** You move, resize, and arrange your video overlays directly with the mouse on screen, just like a PowerPoint slide.
2. **Hassle-free Timeline:** A single key to slice clips instantly, with clips auto-snapping together so you don't leave gaps.
3. **Zero complex settings:** No need to manage nodes, effect channels, or sequence settings just to make a clean edit.

The problem is that it's impossible to use it anywhere other than Windows and macOS, and paying $250 a year is a total dealbreaker for me.

Softwares like Premiere Pro (or FilmCraft) are great for heavy editing, but they quickly feel overly complex when you just want to do a quick edit without hassle. Creating a video editor based on an ergonomics as simple, fast, and smooth as Camtasia, but natively available on Linux, Windows, and Mac, would be awesome.

By the way, if you like the idea, it could for example be called *CamtaCraft* (with maybe a *CaptureCraft* module for recording) to go alongside *FilmCraft*.

title: Proposal: standalone apps with an optional shared workspace, consistent UX and InDesign workflow compatibility

I work in magazine layout, prepress, photography and retouching, with many years of Adobe experience. A few observations from that perspective:

Everyone understandably wants their favourite application added. But trying to cover everything risks the same development hell that, in my view, Adobe has reached: doing everything and too often nothing properly.

I’m not qualified to set your priorities, but I wonder how much effort it makes sense to invest in areas already served extremely well by DaVinci Resolve.


**Standalone apps, shared workspace**

Following the discussion in #2242, could the architecture support both standalone applications and optional modules within one shared workspace?

Combining LightCraft and PhotoCraft seems particularly promising: a substantial photographic catalogue, RAW development and layered retouching, with coherent metadata, version management, batch processing and export. Users could install either application separately or use both together.

title: [All apps] Web build: detect, remember and centrally set the interface language
author: johancoppens
body:
Organisations that serve the web builds from their own server (schools, companies) need the interface in their users' language without asking every user to change a setting in every app. Today that isn't possible:

- the web build doesn't detect the browser language: `docs/localization.md` in PhotoCraft says Auto stays English "until browser-locale detection is implemented";
- each app keeps its own preferences in `localStorage` (for example `photocraft.preferences`), so a user picks the language again in every app;
- on shared or managed devices, such as school Chromebooks, `localStorage` can be cleared between sessions, so a user's choice can't be the only mechanism.

Our case: we're a school group in Flanders serving the unmodified web releases to students' Chromebooks, and we want them in Dutch (`nl-BE`), which PhotoCraft already has and other apps are getting.

## Proposal: resolve the language in this order

1. **The user's own choice**, saved once for the whole suite. Apps served from the same origin could share one key (for example `craft.language`), so choosing a language in one app applies to all of them.
2. **A site configuration from the host**, for example a `craft-config.json` fetched from the site root (or next to `index.html`), with the organisation's defaults:
   ```json
   { "language": "nl-BE", "lockLanguage": false }
   ```
   With `lockLanguage: true`, the language choice is hidden and the configured language always applies. A missing or invalid file is ignored.
3. **A URL parameter** such as `?lang=nl-BE`, so links and installed web apps (manifest `start_url`) can choose a language.
4. **The browser's languages** (`navigator.languages`), matched against the registered catalogs the same way the desktop builds match the system language. On managed devices, admins already set these centrally through Chrome's language policies.
5. English.

The same configuration file could later carry other organisation defaults (units, paper size), but language i…

title: [All apps] Dutch interface for Flanders and the Netherlands: an nl base with an nl-BE layer
author: johancoppens
body:
Dutch is the language of about 24 million people in Belgium (Flanders) and the Netherlands. We are a school group in Flanders and host the web builds of the Craft apps for our students' Chromebooks. This issue covers the Dutch interface across the suite. Language selection in the web build (storytold/artcraft#2405) and Dutch spelling (storytold/wordcraft#2505) have their own issues.

## Where it stands

- **PhotoCraft** has a complete Dutch catalog (storytold/photocraft#1877, merged). It uses the informal "je", and `nl-NL` and `nl-BE` both resolve to it.
- **WordCraft** has two Dutch catalogs waiting: storytold/wordcraft#1070 (formal "u") and storytold/wordcraft#2139 (a user's `nl.tsv`).
- **The other apps** (VectorCraft, FilmCraft, LightCraft, PdfCraft, EffectCraft, DesignCraft, DeckCraft, GridCraft, CADCraft, SoundCraft, FigCraft and the launcher) have no Dutch interface yet. Related: storytold/artcraft#2217, storytold/pdfcraft#1546, storytold/vectorcraft#2393, storytold/pdfcraft#2183, storytold/craft-launcher#453.

## An `nl` base with an `nl-BE` layer

Menus and dialogs read the same in Flanders and the Netherlands, so most of the work is one shared `nl` catalog. The two regions do differ in a few places:

- **Dates:** `nl-BE` writes 16/10/2026, `nl-NL` writes 16-10-2026 (numbers and euro amounts are the same). This matters for date cells in GridCraft and date fields in WordCraft and DeckCraft.
- **Vocabulary**, mostly in templates, sample content and a few labels: for example leerkracht / docent, punten / cijfers, rekenblad / spreadsheet.

We'd suggest:
- one `nl` catalog per app, and an `nl-BE` catalog that holds only the strings that differ and falls back to `nl` for the rest (`nl-NL` = `nl`);
- date and time formats following the full tag (`nl-BE` / `nl-NL`), not just the language;
- both offered in the language menu, for example "Nederlands (België)" and "Nederlands (Nederland)".

A full separate Flemish catalog would double the work and drift apart; `nl` a…

title: [RFC] Suite-wide Host Mode: Remote UI, Multi-Surface Workspaces and Hybrid Rendering
author: daro93
body:
## Summary

I would like to suggest a suite-wide architecture feature rather than an app-specific feature:

**Any native Craft application could optionally act as an application host and expose its full UI — or individual UI surfaces/panels — to browsers and other devices.**

This should not be implemented as "RDP in a browser".

Craft is in a unique position because many of the applications already exist both as native desktop applications and as browser/WASM applications, while more shared runtime, UI, collaboration and control infrastructure is being developed across the suite.

Combining these pieces could create something significantly more powerful than conventional remote desktop software and could become a major differentiator for Craft very early in its development.

---

## 1. Native Craft application as the authoritative host

A user could run FilmCraft, SoundCraft, PhotoCraft, DeckCraft, WordCraft, etc. normally on a workstation.

The native application remains authoritative and keeps:

- the actual project/document state
- local files and NAS/file-server access
- native plugins
- CPU/GPU resources
- caches
- high-resolution media
- fonts
- audio/video hardware
- local devices

The application could optionally enable something like:

**Host Remote Surfaces / Share UI**

```text
Native Craft application
│
├─ project / document
├─ local files / NAS
├─ CPU / GPU / plugins
├─ normal local desktop UI
│
└─ Craft Remote Surface Host
   │
   ├─ Full UI
   ├─ Timeline
   ├─ Mixer
   ├─ Preview
   ├─ Properties
   └─ other app-specific surfaces
```

A browser on another computer, tablet or phone could connect over LAN, VPN or optionally a future Craft collaboration service.

This would allow someone to start working at a workstation, move to a tablet on the sofa or in the garden, and continue the exact same running session.

No second copy of the project needs to be opened and no cloud-file synchronization is required.

---

## 2. Multi-Surface, not screen sharing…

However, if you attempt to open the launcher again via its desktop/taskbar shortcut, it spawns a completely new instance of the application instead of restoring the window from the system tray. title: [Bug] PDFCraft fails to render PDFs with a large number of pages
author: JoaoMarcosVilela
body:
# [Bug] PDFCraft fails to render PDFs with a large number of pages

## Bug Description
When opening a PDF document containing a large number of pages, PDFCraft fails to render the content properly. The pages appear in the interface but remain blank, without displaying their actual content.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open PDFCraft.
2. Select a PDF file containing a large number of pages.
3. Wait for the document to load.
4. Notice that the pages appear blank instead of displaying their content.

## Expected Behavior
PDFCraft should correctly render all pages of a PDF document, regardless of the number of pages, while maintaining reasonable performance and smooth navigation.

## Actual Behavior
When loading large PDF documents, PDFCraft fails to render the page content, displaying only blank pages.

## Suggested Improvements
Investigate the rendering process for large PDF documents and consider implementing performance optimizations, such as:

- **Lazy loading:** Render pages only when needed.
- **On-demand rendering:** Prioritize rendering visible pages.
- **Memory management:** Optimize memory usage when handling large documents.
- **Caching:** Improve the caching strategy for rendered pages.

## Environment
- **Application:** PDFCraft
- **Project:** ArtCraft
- **Version:** To be determined
- **Operating System:** To be determined

## Suggested Labels
`bug` `performance` `pdf-rendering`

title: GUI Corruption and System Freeze After Resume from Suspend / Idle State (Affects most apps except VectorCraft)
author: AmrTarekElaasy
body: 1. Environment Details * Tested Operating Systems: Fedora Workstation, Ubuntu * Tested Package Formats: AppImage, Flatpak, .deb * Graphics Hardware: NVIDIA / Intel Integrated Graphics 2. Scope & Affected Applications * Affected Applications: The vast majority of ArtCraft applications exhibit these rendering and stability bugs. * Exception: VectorCraft works normally and does not experience these UI corruption or freeze issues. 3. Detailed Description of Issues Issue 1: GUI Corruption After Resuming from Suspend (AppImage) * Steps to Reproduce: * Launch the application (AppImage format). * Put the system into Suspend / Sleep mode. * Wake the system back up. * Actual Result: The application's window/UI becomes completely corrupted, visually broken, and fails to redraw, forcing a forced close and restart of the application. Issue 2: Random GUI Corruption During Idle/Active Use (Flatpak) * Steps to Reproduce: * Launch the Flatpak version of the application on Fedora. * Leave the application open (idle or active use). * Actual Result: The UI suddenly corrupts and breaks on its own without any explicit system power state change. Issue 3: Complete System Freeze During Suspend (.deb Package on Ubuntu) * Steps to Reproduce: * Install and launch the .deb package of the application on Ubuntu. * Trigger a system Suspend / Sleep. * Actual Result: The entire system hangs and hard freezes during the suspend transition, requiring a manual forced power-off via the physical power button. 4. Preliminary Technical Context * The issues appear to be directly related to how the applications handle hardware acceleration and GPU context loss (OpenGL / Vulkan context loss) during display server state changes (Wayland / X11) and system power management state transitions.
