title: [Feature Request] Add official NetBSD support and binaries for the ArtCraft ecosystem
author: amapekibert
body:
### Type of Request
Enhancement / Feature Request

### Description
I would like to officially request NetBSD support for PhotoCraft and the rest of the ArtCraft ecosystem apps (VectorCraft, FilmCraft, LightCraft, PdfCraft, EffectCraft, DesignCraft). 

Since FreeBSD is already officially supported with native x86_64 tarball builds, expanding the BSD family support to NetBSD (`pkgsrc`) would be an incredible addition for users running lightweight, secure Unix-like operating systems on desktop hardware and laptops.

### Why this is feasible
1. **Pure Rust Architecture:** As per `AGENTS.md`, the ecosystem is built natively in 100% pure Rust (using `egui`/`eframe` and `wgpu`) without any bloated JavaScript/TypeScript or Electron/Tauri dependencies. Rust has excellent support for NetBSD.
2. **Graphics Stack Compatibility:** NetBSD features a highly robust graphics layer supporting X11/Wayland and modern Vulkan drivers, which aligns perfectly with your `wgpu` rendering pipeline.
3. **Cross-Platform Parity:** Sister operating systems like MidnightBSD and FreeBSD are already enjoying native ports and official binary releases.

### Proposed Solution
- Include a NetBSD build target (`x86_64-unknown-netbsd`) in the GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows.
- Provide official `photocraft-<ver>-netbsd-x86_64.tar.gz` pre-compiled binaries in the GitHub Releases section, similar to the current FreeBSD implementation.
- Cooperate with or provide a baseline structure for the NetBSD community to easily maintain `graphics/photocraft` inside the official `pkgsrc` / `pkgsrc-wip` repositories.

Thank you and all the 200+ human contributors for building such a blazing-fast, open-source alternative to proprietary creative suites!

title: Feature Request / Bug: Missing or broken Auto-fill / Series drag-to-increment across multiple rows
author: amrali-tec
body:
Summary
The auto-fill / fill handle feature (similar to Microsoft Excel's drag-to-fill functionality) is either missing or failing to generate automated numerical/pattern sequences across multiple rows.

Problem Description
When selecting a cell or a range of cells containing sequential data (e.g., 1, 2, 3 or dates) and dragging the selection handle downwards across multiple rows, the application does not automatically increment the series.

Instead, it either copies the exact same value across all rows (duplicate fill) or does not provide a fill-handle handle at all to drag down across multiple rows.

Expected Behavior
Series Increment: Dragging down from a single cell or a sequence (e.g., highlighting 1 and 2 and dragging) should intelligently increment subsequent cells (3, 4, 5...).

Multi-Row Support: The auto-fill handle should seamlessly extend sequences across any number of selected rows.

Auto-fill Options: Similar to Excel, providing a contextual dropdown after dragging (e.g., Copy Cells, Fill Series, Fill Formatting Only) would allow users to choose the desired fill behavior.

Steps to Reproduce
Open a sheet in GridCraft.

Enter 1 in row 1 and 2 in row 2.

Select both cells and attempt to drag the bottom-right corner handle downwards across multiple rows.

Observed Result: The series does not increment automatically across the target rows.

title: [Feature Request] Seamless vector-to-motion workflow between VectorCraft and EffectCraft (Overlord-style bridge)
author: martibrustudio-oss
body:
### Summary / Feature Description
As a designer working with vector graphics and animation, having a seamless bridge between vector editing tools (**VectorCraft**) and motion design software (**EffectCraft**) — similar to the **Overlord** workflow between Illustrator and After Effects — dramatically speeds up production.

Currently, transferring vector shapes into animation software often requires exporting intermediate files (SVG, EPS, .ai ), re-importing them, and manually reorganizing layers or converting them into editable shape paths.

### Proposed Solution
Implement an integrated one-click sync/bridge functionality between VectorCraft and EffectCraft.

Key capabilities for this bridge:
* **One-Click Push:** A dedicated button/shortcut to send selected vector shapes and text elements directly to the active EffectCraft composition.
* **Preserve Visual Properties & Styles:** Full fidelity preservation of original vector paths, gradient fills, strokes, opacity, color swatches, anchor points, and layer names.
* **Editable Text Layers:** Text elements should transfer either as native live editable text layers or optionally converted into outlines/shape paths.
* **Flexible Layering Options (Import Modes):**
  * **Split Layers:** Import elements as individual, separated layers for full animation control.
  * **Single Layer / Grouped:** Import selected elements combined into a single shape group/layer to keep the timeline clean.
* **Editable Shape Layers:** Vectors should arrive as native, editable motion paths ready for keyframing in EffectCraft.

### UX / Workflow Integration
1. Select one or multiple vector/text elements in VectorCraft.
2. Choose the transfer mode (e.g., *Split Layers* vs. *Grouped*, *Live Text* vs. *Outlines*).
3. Click the sync icon or press a shortcut (e.g., `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P`).
4. The selected elements immediately instantiate as editable native layers in the active EffectCraft composition at the current playhead position.

title: [Feature Request] VectorCraft to PhotoCraft Copy & Paste (Smart Objects, Shape & Text Support)
author: martibrustudio-oss
body:
### Summary / Feature Description
Currently, copying elements from **PhotoCraft** and pasting them into **VectorCraft** works natively — preserving editable text and shape elements. However, copying vector shapes or text in **VectorCraft** and attempting to paste them into **PhotoCraft** does not work.

Since cross-app parsing for text and vector data already exists in one direction, bringing full compatibility from VectorCraft to PhotoCraft is essential for a complete workflow.

### Technical Context (Investigation)
Looking into the codebase, copying elements currently relies on an internal local state clipboard (`state.clipboard` inside `useSceneStore` / Zustand) rather than interfacing with the system clipboard natively. Extending this mechanism to support system-wide or cross-module clipboard persistence (similar to how text/vectors are parsed internally) will enable seamless data transfer between VectorCraft and PhotoCraft.

### Proposed Solution
Enable full clipboard compatibility when pasting vector content from VectorCraft into PhotoCraft (`Cmd/Ctrl + V`).

Users should be able to choose how the content is inserted:
1. **Vector / Shape Layer:** Editable native vector paths.
2. **Live Text Layer:** Preserves editable text and formatting.
3. **Pixels / Raster Layer:** Rasterizes the selection at canvas resolution.
4. **Smart Object / Linked Vector (Non-destructive):** Embeds or links the VectorCraft asset so double-clicking it opens VectorCraft to edit and update automatically.

### UX / Workflow Integration
1. Select and copy (`Cmd/Ctrl + C`) elements in VectorCraft.
2. Switch to PhotoCraft and paste (`Cmd/Ctrl + V`).
3. Choose the desired format (*Shape / Live Text / Pixels / Smart Vector Object*) from a quick popup or option bar.
4. Asset is placed on the canvas.

### Why this matters
Non-destructive workflows and smart vector objects are foundational for branding, mockups, and UI design. Completing this bridge across both applications makes the suite fully…

## ELI5
IntelliJ IDEA is the workbench most Java developers live in, but it is heavy. JavaCraft would be a fast, native, low-memory IDE for Java and Kotlin projects that does the everyday work well: read, navigate, run, debug and review code.

## Motivation
- IntelliJ IDEA routinely uses several GB of RAM; a pure-Rust native app could stay in the hundreds of MB
- Many developers mostly need an IDE to understand, run and review code, not every feature IntelliJ has
- Should be native on Linux, macOS and Windows. Existing lightweight attempts such as [Lithe](https://github.com/1lck/Lithe-IDEA) ship only for macOS and Windows
- Fits the Craft apps approach: a focused, from-scratch alternative to a heavyweight tool

## Must-have features
- Runs natively on macOS, Linux and Windows, with release builds for all three
- Java (and ideally Kotlin) code intelligence: go to definition, find usages, rename, diagnostics (e.g. via a language server such as jdtls, started on demand)
- Maven and Gradle: import projects, run goals and tasks
- Run and debug configurations, including Spring Boot apps (JDWP debugger, breakpoints, variables)
- Test runner for JUnit
- Git: changes view, side-by-side diff review, branches
- Integrated terminal
- Database tool for browsing tables and running SQL

## Nice to have
- Opens an existing IntelliJ project (`.idea`) without conversion
- IntelliJ-compatible keymap
- Local history

# NovelCraft – Open-source novel writing & planning(Scrivener alternative)

## Description

I would like to propose **NovelCraft**, an open-source alternative to **Scrivener**, designed specifically for novelists, authors, and long-form fiction writers.

Unlike StoryCraft, which focuses on screenwriting and storyboards (#2166 ), NovelCraft would provide a dedicated environment for planning, organizing, writing, and publishing novels.

## Suggested Features

- **Project organization:** Hierarchical chapters, scenes, folders, and drag-and-drop reordering.
- **Writing environment:** Distraction-free editor, word count goals, notes, and revision tracking.
- **Story planning:** Corkboard, character sheets, worldbuilding, timelines, and relationship maps.
- **Research management:** Integrated references, images, documents, and research notes.
- **Publishing:** Export to DOCX, EPUB, PDF, and Markdown.

## ArtCraft Ecosystem Integration

NovelCraft could reuse **WordCraft** for document editing and integrate with **DesignCraft** for professional book layout, typography, and publishing.

Optional AI-assisted tools could support brainstorming, consistency checks, and manuscript analysis while keeping authors in full control of their work.

**Goal:** Create a complete, open-source writing ecosystem that takes an author from the first idea to a professionally published book.

title: [VectorCraft] Font glyphs missing and auto-converted to curves when opening .ai files
author: solowinskiwork
body:
markdown
### Description
When opening an Adobe Illustrator (.ai) file, VectorCraft fails to read the full character/glyph palette of the installed font. Characters that are not recognized by the app are automatically converted into vector curves (outlines), making the text uneditable. 

Interestingly, these exact fonts and characters render perfectly fine as live, editable text in both Adobe Illustrator and Affinity Designer.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a text object in Adobe Illustrator or Affinity using a font with an extended glyph set.
2. Save/Export the file as `.ai`.
3. Open the `.ai` file in VectorCraft.

### Expected Behavior
VectorCraft should recognize the full font palette, keep the text live and editable, and preserve all character glyphs.

### Actual Behavior
Unrecognized glyphs are stripped from the live text layout and automatically baked/expanded into raw vector paths (curves).

### Environment
- OS: [Mac OS 27.0.1]
- ArtCraft ver. 0.13.1

title: OneDrive sync client for Linux as a new Craft app
author: gsilano
body:
Hi! With WordCraft and DeckCraft, the Craft suite is close to being a full Microsoft 365 alternative on Linux. One gap remains: OneDrive has no official Linux client, so users can’t easily open and save their cloud files.

**Idea:** A native Rust app that syncs OneDrive (personal and work/school) via the Microsoft Graph API, with selective sync, Files-On-Demand, SharePoint support, a tray GUI, and direct integration with the other Craft apps.

**Homework:** I searched open and closed issues and found no existing request. Tools like abraunegg/onedrive, onedriver, and rclone exist, but they are mostly CLI-based and not integrated with an office suite.

**Existing solutions:**
- [abraunegg/onedrive](https://github.com/abraunegg/onedrive) (“OneDrive Client for Linux”) is the most mature and widely used option. It is free and actively maintained, supporting OneDrive Personal, OneDrive for Business, Microsoft 365, and SharePoint document libraries. Its features include real-time local file monitoring with inotify, real-time syncing of remote changes via webhooks, and resumable uploads. It is still actively developed, and version 2.5.11 was released on June 30. Its main limitation is that it is a command-line tool, although a separate community project called OneDriveGUI provides a graphical front end for it.
- [onedriver (jstaf)](https://github.com/jstaf/onedriver) takes a different approach. It mounts OneDrive as a filesystem and downloads files only when you open them, which is close to Windows’ Files-On-Demand. It has a simple GUI, but the maintainer has said that shared items and SharePoint support required significant changes that were still in progress. The project also looks less active lately, with packaging requests for newer Ubuntu releases left waiting.
- **GNOME Online Accounts** has added OneDrive support in recent versions, which lets you browse files in Nautilus without syncing them locally.
- **Commercial clients** such as **Insync** and **ExpanDrive** off…

title: Linux AppImage cannot discover system GStreamer plugins; WebKit aborts and UI becomes unresponsive
author: BSTail
body:
### Summary

ArtCraft 0.42.0, built using the unchanged official
`script/artcraft/unix_build.sh`, produces an AppImage that cannot find
GStreamer plugins already installed on the host.

The default launch produced WebKit renderer aborts and an unresponsive
interface. Launching the same AppImage with explicit system GStreamer
plugin and scanner paths resolved the observed problems in one interactive
test: clicking, typing, and account creation all worked.

This identifies a plugin-discovery defect and a successful workaround.
It does not yet prove that every observed renderer abort has the same cause.

### Environment

- Omarchy / Arch Linux
- Kernel: 7.2.8-9-omarchy
- Hyprland 0.56.2, Wayland
- Intel Core Ultra 7 258V, integrated Intel Arc graphics
- Display: 2560×1600, scale 2
- ArtCraft: 0.42.0
- Source commit: 40e04793b504147de97ba1f0659d3975167524e5
- Built with `script/artcraft/unix_build.sh`
- Tauri CLI: 2.12.4
- WebKitGTK: 2.54.1
- GStreamer: 1.28.8
- gst-plugins-base and gst-plugins-good installed

Application stderr includes:

```text
GStreamer element appsink not found. Please install it.
GStreamer element appsrc not found. Please install it
GStreamer element autoaudiosink not found. Please install it
```

GLib/GStreamer object assertions follow. Three WebKitWebProcess SIGABRT
coredumps were recorded during the affected launches.

The AppImage contains GStreamer libraries but no

title: [Windows] Tool updates always need admin (UAC): offer per-user install for the tool MSIs
author: colestevenson97
body:
Problem
On Windows, every update of a Craft tool shows the UAC admin prompt. With frequent releases, that is a prompt every few days.

The launcher does not have this problem. It installs per-user and updates without a prompt. The 7 tool MSIs install per-machine only.

## What I found (Windows 11 Pro 26200, launcher 0.6.1)
| Package | ALLUSERS | Summary Info Word Count | Installs to |
|---|---|---|---|
| ArtCraft Launcher 0.6.1 | not set | 10 (elevation not required) | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs` |
| VectorCraft 0.14.0 | 1 | 2 (elevation required) | `C:\Program Files` |

PhotoCraft, GridCraft, PdfCraft, SoundCraft, DeckCraft and WordCraft are registered per-machine the same way.

Request
Make the tool MSIs dual-purpose, the same as the launcher can be:
- `ALLUSERS=2` with `MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1` as the default when installed through the launcher, and Word Count bit 3 set, so per-user installs and updates need no admin.
- Keep the per-machine install available (`ALLUSERS=1`) for admins who want Program Files. This also covers #2199.
- Have the launcher update a tool in the same scope it was installed in.

Workaround I use today
A Task Scheduler task that starts the launcher with highest privileges. It works, but the launcher and every tool then run as admin, and drag and drop from Explorer stops working.

title: bugs wordcraft
author: abu-faqih
body:
# 🐛 Wordcraft — Table Editor Bugs

## Bug #1 — Paste from external table only fills one cell
**Steps:** Copy a 3x3 range from Excel/Sheets → paste into a 3x3 Wordcraft table.
**Expected:** Data spreads across cells by row/column.
**Actual:** Everything dumps into a single cell.
**Fix hint:** Parse `text/html` (`<table>`) and `text/plain` (split on `\t` and `\n`) in the paste handler; distribute into target cells.

---

## Bug #2 — Vertical merge also merges the column to the right
**Steps:** Select 2 cells vertically (e.g. B1+B2) → Merge.
**Expected:** Only B1+B2 merge; column C untouched.
**Actual:** Column C also merges / layout shifts.
**Fix hint:** Audit `mergeCells()` — check `colspan`/`rowspan` math and grid re-indexing after merge; likely iterating `col + 1` incorrectly.

---

## Bug #3 — Cannot set borders per side
**Steps:** Select a cell → open border panel.
**Expected:** Control `top/right/bottom/left` individually — thickness, color, style per side.
**Actual:** Only global/all-sides border (or none). Can't e.g. shrink one side only.
**Fix hint:** Store border per cell as `{ top, right, bottom, left }` objects; render with `borderTop`/`borderRight`/etc. instead of `border` shorthand. Add per-side controls in the UI panel.

---

**Priority:** Bug #2 (High — corrupts table), Bug #1 (High — breaks workflow), Bug #3 (Medium — formatting limitation).

title: Cross-app linked files: place PhotoCraft/VectorCraft files as updatable links in VectorCraft/PhotoCraft/DesignCraft
author: ktheunlikedoll
body:
## Summary

Requesting **cross-compatibility between the ArtCraft apps**: files from PhotoCraft and VectorCraft should be usable as **linked files** in VectorCraft, PhotoCraft, and DesignCraft — placed into a document as a live reference to the source file, not just a flattened/embedded copy.

## The workflow this unlocks

Being able to place linked files from another application in the same family makes keeping those files updated much easier across the whole suite:

- Place a **PhotoCraft** file (`.pcraft` / layered raster) into a **VectorCraft** document as a link → edit the image in PhotoCraft → the VectorCraft document updates.
- Place a **VectorCraft** file (`.vectorcraft` / SVG) into **PhotoCraft** as a link → revise the vector art once → every placed instance updates.
- Place linked vector + raster assets into **DesignCraft** layouts — the family's "publisher" is the natural aggregator for pages composed of assets maintained in the other apps.

## Why it matters

This is much like **Adobe's cross-compatibility** (linked files across Illustrator/Photoshop/InDesign), which is what the family is clearly going for. Linked assets create a single source of truth: each asset is edited in the app best suited to it, and every document that uses it stays current — no manual re-export and re-place after every change. For multi-asset work (layouts, posters, branding systems, decks) this would be a **huge boon to the family as a whole**: five great apps become one connected pipeline.

## Suggested mechanics (for discussion)

- The place/import flow accepts sibling-app native files and records a **link** (source path, sync state/hash) instead of only embedding content.
- On open: detect changed sources and offer **"Update links"**; graceful missing-file state with a relink/locate action.
- A small **Links panel**: placed links with status (up to date / modified / missing) and per-link actions (update, relink, embed to break the link).
- Links resolve at export/print time.…

title: [Tooling & Suite Infrastructure] artcraft-command-bridge - a command-level aggregate MCP for the Crafting Apps (5 tools instead of 799)
author: xiewg1987
body:
## Summary

Connecting the Crafting Apps to an MCP client the way their own MCP servers expect costs **799 tools / 547 KB of schema ≈ 140k tokens of permanently resident context**. This is a thin aggregation layer that drives the apps' CLIs instead and exposes **5 tools / 3.5 KB**.

Repo: https://github.com/xiewg1987/artcraft-command-bridge — MIT, Node ≥ 18, zero runtime dependencies.

## The problem, measured

Registering each app's own MCP server (`<app>-cli mcp`) and calling `tools/list`:

| app | tools | schema |
|---|---|---|
| LightCraft | 388 | 203.6 KB |
| PdfCraft | 175 | 170.3 KB |
| VectorCraft | 32 | 33.0 KB |
| EffectCraft | 27 | 24.0 KB |
| DesignCraft | 26 | 18.5 KB |
| PhotoCraft | 25 | 25.1 KB |
| DeckCraft | 25 | 15.3 KB |
| GridCraft | 21 | 15.9 KB |
| FigCraft | 18 | 17.2 KB |
| FilmCraft | 17 | 9.9 KB |
| SoundCraft | 17 | 4.0 KB |
| WordCraft | 16 | 5.8 KB |
| CADCraft | 12 | 4.6 KB |
| **total** | **799** | **547.3 KB** |

MCP has no "give me the names, fetch the schema when I call it" mode — the client takes the whole `tools/list` result and keeps every `name` + `description` + `inputSchema` resident, re-sent on every request. Clients that do have on-demand tool search don't help here: that covers deferred tools (cron, integrations), not MCP server tools.

## What already exists, and why this is different

- **artcraft-toolbox** (#2343) — a suite *manager*: download, verify, update, launch. Complementary rather than overlapping; the toolbox gets the apps onto the machine, this makes them pleasant to drive.
- **claude-storytold-skills** — solves the same goal at the *skill* layer: per-app skills that grep generated reference catalogs instead of reading them whole. But it still registers each app's MCP server with `claude mcp add`, so the tool schemas stay resident — the skill list is ~2.3k tokens, the tools are ~140k.
- **eznix86/mcp-gateway** — a general gateway with the same shape, but it aggregates *MCP servers*, so all 13 upstream processe…

title: [Feature request] A CSP-style illustration mode for PhotoCraft, or the ability to import .sut and .brushset brushes
author: betzadev
body:
PhotoCraft already covers the Photoshop side of a digital artist's workflow.
What's still missing is the other half: **Clip Studio Paint-style illustration.**

I'd love to see PhotoCraft grow an illustration mode built around the
features that make CSP irreplaceable for comic and concept artists:

- **Stabilized brush engine** with real pen pressure, tilt, and rotation support
- **Dual-stamp brushes** (stroke + texture) with editable dynamics
- **Rulers**: straight line, curve, ellipse, multi-point perspective, radial symmetry
- **Editable vector lines after the stroke** — adjusting width per control point,
  exactly like CSP's line correction tool
- **`.clip` file import/export**, the same way PSD support exists today

I know this is a big ask — a full CSP equivalent is years of work, and it may
well belong in its own app someday (DrawCraft?). But I wanted to put the
request on the record.

If a full clone is out of scope, I'd happily settle for a much smaller
beginning: **importing Procreate (`.brushset`) and Clip Studio Paint (`.sut`)
brushes into PhotoCraft.**

Losing a carefully built brush library is the single biggest reason artists
hesitate to switch tools — and no open-source app imports these formats today.
Even an approximate mapping, with a report of what carried over and what
didn't, would be enough to bring a lot of illustrators through the door.

Either way, thank you for building this 💕

I would like to request Arabic language support in ArtCraft. Arabic is spoken by millions of people, but many of them still face difficulties using creative software because the interface is not available in their native language.

Adding Arabic support would make ArtCraft more accessible to Arabic-speaking users and help more people discover and use your applications. Ideally, this would include a fully translated interface and proper right-to-left (RTL) support.

I believe open-source software should be accessible to everyone, regardless of their language. I hope you will consider adding Arabic to your future localization plans.

Thank you for your time and for your efforts in the open-source community.

Best regards,
An Arabic-speaking user

title: Infrared Photo Editing in Art Craft
author: davidgrahamsites
body:
In professional raw editors like Adobe Camera Raw and Lightroom, the infrared editing workflow relies fundamentally on custom digital negative profiles (.dcp) to overcome the hardware-calculated limitations of standard raw color engines. Because straight-from-camera infrared files suffer from an extreme, overpowering red or pink color cast, standard white balance tools—which generally cap out at a minimum color temperature of 2000K—lack the range necessary to neutralize the image. Adobe addresses this by allowing users to map a custom camera profile generated via the Adobe DNG Profile Editor, which shifts the internal temperature scale matrix downward by an offset of -50 to -100. Once this custom profile is applied in Adobe Camera Raw, the white balance eyedropper gains the required headroom to sample green foliage and successfully neutralize it to a clean, glowing white. From this neutral base, the image is passed into Photoshop where a Channel Mixer adjustment layer is used to completely swap the Red and Blue channels (setting Red to 100% Blue, and Blue to 100% Red), transforming the muddy copper tones into vibrant blue skies and completing the iconic false-color infrared aesthetic.

Basically we need the ability to add our custom camera profiles into the editing app. If you could do this directly in art craft instead of requiring a Camera Raw like feature, I would wash your car for a month!A

title: [Bug] Desktop shortcuts move under the Recycle Bin during updates, shifting all other desktop icons (ArtCraft Launcher & PdfCraft)
author: Hachibi91
body:
### **Description**
Hello,

When updating your software (specifically ArtCraft Launcher and PdfCraft—the only two programs from your suite that I use), the desktop shortcut icons systematically move and reposition themselves directly underneath the Recycle Bin, behaving as if a brand-new shortcut had just been added to a desktop with no icons (apart from the Recycle Bin).

As a result, this pushes and shifts all other desktop icons out of place, completely breaking my desktop layout.

For context, these are the only applications on my machine that exhibit this behavior, which suggests an issue specific to your installer or update script (e.g., deleting and recreating shortcuts during update instead of preserving them).

### **Steps to Reproduce**
1. Have ArtCraft Launcher and/or PdfCraft desktop shortcuts placed at a custom location alongside other desktop icons.

2. Trigger an update for either of these applications (in my case, via the in-app updater of the ArtCraft Launcher).

3. Observe the desktop layout once the update is completed.

### **Expected Behavior**
The software icons should retain their original positions on the Desktop after an update without disturbing the overall desktop icon arrangement.

### **Actual Behavior**
The icons are forcibly moved underneath the Recycle Bin, shifting all other desktop icons and forcing me to manually re-organize my entire desktop after every update.

### **Environment / Additional Context**

- **Software affected:** ArtCraft Launcher & PdfCraft (the only two tools from your suite I use)

- **OS:** Windows 11

- **Additional notes:** No other software installed on my PC causes this desktop icon displacement.

body:

title: Feature Suggestion: Dynamic Engineering Notebook / Math Pad App (Calcpad alternative)
author: wwwlmnop12345-dev
body:
### Type of Request
New Tool / Major Suite Expansion

### Description
First of all, thank you for your incredible work on the ArtCraft suite. Building high-performance creative tools in Rust is a game-changer!

I would like to politely suggest a new addition to the suite—or a major feature extension—inspired by mathematical and engineering notebooks like Calcpad or Blockpad. It would be amazing to have a modern, Rust-powered alternative that combines markdown writing, live mathematical evaluation, and interactive geometry.

### Core Capabilities Requested
* **Natural Math Notation:** An intuitive interface where users can write mathematical relationships naturally and non-programmatically (feeling like standard equations rather than software code).
* **Standard Assignment:** A math parser that uses the regular equals sign (`=`) for assigning variables and defining formulas, rather than the programming-style assignment operator (`:=`).
* **Parametric Geometric Drawing:** The ability to sketch 2D/3D geometric shapes directly inside the document workspace.
* **Live Variable Binding:** Linking these geometric shapes directly to the mathematical variables. Changing a dimension value in the calculations should automatically update the size/scale of the drawn shape in real-time, and vice versa.
* **Professional Export Options:** Seamless document compilation with the ability to export the final reports directly to Microsoft Word (`.docx`) and PDF formats while perfectly preserving equation layout and text formatting.

### Technical context / Benefits
Given your team's expertise in building powerful visual, vector, and desktop tools using Rust, a dedicated tool like this (perhaps named **MathCraft** or **EngCraft**) would perfectly bridge the gap between technical calculations and graphic documentation. It would be an incredibly fast, lightweight, and modern alternative for engineers, scientists, and students.
